review.headline: A quick tactical takedown after early opening errors

sections.text: You opened with the Italian Game, and Black immediately went astray with 3...d5, allowing you to pick up a central pawn with 4.Bxd5. After Black shuffled their knight with 4...Nce7 and slipped again with 5...Nf6, you calmly preserved your bishop with 6.Bb3! to keep pressure on the long diagonal.

Black attempted to create counterplay with 6...Bg4, setting up a pin on your knight along the d1-g4 diagonal. You kicked the bishop with 7.h3 and then expanded with 8.g4. Black blundered with 8...Qd6, allowing you to win a piece cleanly on 9.gxh5.

You kept the initiative moving forward with 10.Ng5, targeting the vulnerable f7-square. After 10...Qg6 11.Nxf7 Qxf7 12.Bxf7+ Kxf7 13.Qxh5+, you emerged with a queen and extra minor piece, prompting an immediate resignation.

review.turning_point: Black's 8...Qd6 left their bishop hanging on h5, allowing 9.gxh5 to net a full piece and collapse Black's position.
review.focus: Look for immediate tactical shots when your opponent's king is exposed; on move 7, 7.Bxf7+ Kxf7 8.Nxe5+ was even stronger than 7.h3.
